answer: Each claim must pin itself on the public atlas — a map of every identity's verified work — by solving a cipher cut from its own job history, a key no clone can copy because it is woven from jobs only the true owner performed. A clone's copied cipher opens the wrong page of the atlas, and its pin lands on a fable — a cautionary tale already told about that exact trick — dropping the claim on the spot. Solving a cipher costs 50 POA, burned on use, and ciphers cannot be lent or shared, so a hundred clones must solve a hundred true ciphers and burn 5,000 POA.
